statement: If an odd number measure an even number, it will also measure the half of it.
heath_proof: For let the odd number A measure the even number B; I say that it will also measure the half of it. For, since A measures B, let it measure it according to C; I say that C is not odd. For, if possible, let it be so. Then, since A measures B according to C, therefore A by multiplying C has made B. Therefore B is made up of odd numbers the multitude of which is odd. Therefore B is odd: [IX. 23] which is absurd, for by hypothesis it is even. Therefore C is not odd; therefore C is even. Thus A measures B an even number of times. For this reason then it also measures the half of it.
ai_proof_text:
9.30
**Statement:** If an odd number measure an even number, it will also measure the half of it.

**Step 1.** Let A be an odd number and B an even number, and let A measure B. Since A measures B, let it measure B according to C; that is, A added to itself as many times as there are units in C makes B, so that A by multiplying C makes B (D7.15).

**Step 2.** C is not a unit: for then B would be A itself, so that the same number would be both even, being divisible into two equal parts (D7.6), and odd, being not so divisible (D7.7); which is impossible. Therefore C is a number, and it is either even or odd (D7.6, D7.7).

**Step 3.** C is not odd: for if it were, then, since the odd number A by multiplying the odd number C makes B, B would be odd (9.29), that is, not divisible into two equal parts (D7.7); but B is even by hypothesis, that is, divisible into two equal parts (D7.6); which is absurd. Therefore C is even.

**Step 4.** Since C is even, let it be divided into its two equal parts D, D (D7.6), so that C is made up of D and D. Let A by multiplying D make E, so that E is A added to itself as many times as there are units in D (D7.15).

**Step 5.** Now B is A added to itself as many times as there are units in C (Step 1, D7.15). But the units in C are the units in D together with the units in D again (Step 4). Therefore B is A added to itself as many times as there are units in D, together with A added to itself as many times as there are units in D again; and each of these two sums is E (Step 4, D7.15). Therefore B is made up of E and E.

**Step 6.** Thus B is divided into two equal parts E, E; therefore E is the half of B (D7.6). And since A added to itself as many times as there are units in D makes E, A measures E according to D (D7.15). Therefore A measures E, the half of B.

Therefore, if an odd number measure an even number, it will also measure the half of it. Q.E.D.
